summary: HD Hyundai and five affiliates are teaming with KCC and underwater robotics firm TAS Global to develop and commercialize a robot- and data-driven Total Hull Care Solution for ships. The system aims to automate the full hull-management cycle, from diagnosing hull condition to cleaning and verifying performance, which would make routine maintenance more measurable and less dependent on manual inspection or ad hoc servicing.

title: People want robots in warehouses and factories, not hospitals or schools, Hexagon study finds
summary: Hexagon’s global Robot Generation study finds that public support for robots is strongest in practical, lower-intimacy settings like warehouses, factories, hazard monitoring, shared-space cleaning, and information lookup, while care roles remain a hard boundary: 68% would prefer robots for heavy lifting, but only 12% for caregiving. The results suggest adoption depends less on blanket enthusiasm than on task context and governance, with 86% saying robots need clear rules, even as children appear markedly more willing than adults to treat robots as workplace colleagues.

extra.full_text: -The sharpest divide is around care: 68% of adults would prefer a robot to handle heavy lifting, but just 12% would choose a robot for caregiving, according to Hexagon's global Robot Generation study. -Adoption is conditional, not universal, as half of adults also prefer robots for monitoring hazards (52%), cleaning shared spaces (50%), and information lookup (50%), but 86% say clear rules for what robots can and can't do are essential. -The next generation is already more comfortable with robots, children are far more open to robots across settings, and are 50% more likely than adults to see robots as "full colleagues" at work.

title: 日 더블기켄, 초소형 액추에이터 모듈 ‘DDM’ 출시
summary: Japan’s Double Giken has started selling the D-Drive Module, an ultra-compact all-in-one actuator for humanoid robots and multi-fingered robot hands. It packages a tiny BLDC motor, high-precision planetary gear reducer, and closed-loop control driver into one module, with feedback for position, speed, temperature, and current, targeting the growing need for smaller, lighter robotic hands as humanoid development accelerates.

title: Qwen-Robot Suite: A Foundation Model Suite for Physical World Intelligence
summary: Qwen-Robot Suite packages Qwen’s embodied-AI stack around two pieces: Qwen-VLA, which turns vision-language inputs into continuous robot actions across manipulation and navigation, and Qwen-RobotWorld, a language-conditioned video world model for predicting physically plausible future trajectories. The release matters because it pushes a single Qwen-based interface across robot embodiments, simulation, planning, and data generation, with reported strong benchmark results such as 97.9% on LIBERO for Qwen-VLA and first-place overall results for Qwen-RobotWorld on EWMBench and DreamGen Bench.

title: Mobileye is entering the US robotaxi market with standalone service
summary: Mobileye plans to launch a standalone robotaxi service in a U.S. city in 2027, using its Moovit mobility platform as the customer-facing layer. The move matters because Mobileye is shifting from supplying autonomy technology to operating a full service in the U.S. robotaxi market, putting it closer to companies that control both the self-driving stack and the rider experience.

extra.full_text: The service will leverage its Moovit platform to launch in an a US city in 2027.

title: IERA Award 2026 Goes to Flying Warehouse Robots by Verity from Switzerland
summary: Verity won the 2026 IERA Award for developing and commercializing a warehouse intelligence system built around flying inventory robots. The system matters because it moves warehouse sensing into autonomous aerial inspection, giving operators a way to track stock and facility state without relying solely on manual scans or fixed infrastructure.

extra.full_text: Verity recognized for development and market launch of warehouse intelligence system

summary: ANYbotics has opened a new engineering and AI hub at DFactory Barcelona, adding a third global location alongside Zurich and San Francisco. The office is meant to expand development capacity for its autonomous robotic inspection systems as demand grows in asset-heavy process industries.

title: The Hidden Lifecycle Challenge Behind Industrial Automation Growth
summary: Industrial automation growth is creating a less visible infrastructure problem: robots, AI systems, and autonomous machines need more capable computing, networking, and lifecycle support than many factories and shipping centers were built to provide. The piece frames automation not just as a productivity upgrade, but as a long-term systems challenge where keeping machines useful, secure, and maintainable may matter as much as deploying them in the first place.

title: "유망 AI 스타트업 최대 1억 지원"...삼성전자 ‘C랩 아웃사이드’ 9기 모집
summary: Samsung Electronics is recruiting the 9th cohort of C-Lab Outside, selecting 30 Korean startups at Series B or earlier across eight areas including AI, robotics, digital health, IoT, mobility, and materials/components. Selected companies, to be announced in November, can receive up to 100 million KRW in support along with PoC collaboration and help reaching global exhibitions, without Samsung taking equity.
